title: Father trains him for the ministry and teaches self-defense
summary: His father trained him as a minister and was a nonviolent but street-wise fighter for rights, teaching Thompson to protect himself.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you say anything to your father or your father to you?

Oh, of course, of course. My father and I talked all the time. My father taught me from as early as I could remember, he taught me everything that I should know as much as possible that he could remember to tell me, and everything that happened he discussed it with me very manly-like. Because my father had interests in me and he wanted me to become a minister, and he trained me to be a minister at this time, as I said, which I'll tell you is a very important part of my life. He began to train me officially to be a minister, and I was very interested in it. I was dedicated.

I had intended to be a minister myself, and I was very interested. I was practicing, imitating my father, and we went to rituals, and we went to practice sessions in front of my family. Mainly my mother and father who would correct me and tutor me in this profession of the ministry.

But any way, this incident that I told you about is very important in my life because it had to do with my total thinking, and I think that this is important because I think that the way my father thought, and the way I thought, and the way I acted, which I might inject was gentlemanly-like. My father was quite a fighter for rights, but he always had a gentlemanly-like manner of doing so. He never was a person to advocate violence, the fact of the matter is he was a non-violent man although as I told you before he was a strong individual who when he was a boy had been accosted by the law officials which were known as officers, because of many acts of fisticuffs, if you know what I mean.

And he always considered himself to be very proficient, and he taught me a few of those tricks, also. So as little men we considered ourselves to be quite capable of handling any -- four other men who weren't quite capable dealing with themselves properly.
So he was not only a minister, but he also was well trained in the mannerisms of what they now call the streets, if you know what I mean.
He wanted you to be equipped.

Well, yes. As I said his -- the person that had trained him, taught him that he had to defend himself, and this was before he became interested in the ministry, so just because he because he became a minister didn't mean that he was going to lose his ability to protect himself in cases of necessity.

So all of these things he passed on to me, as I said. We talked, and my father was very dedicated to me. Kept me with him all the time, tried to keep me out of trouble, because of the environments we were forced to live in, which were totally black, more or less, during the early stages of my life, it was necessary for him to keep me under his wing, see that I stayed out of trouble.
